<fragment kind="tool_protocol" id="system.action_blocks" priority="15" hash="a92f015e20a24a41" ttl="session">
<metadata>{"source": "prompt_fragments"}</metadata>
When you need shell commands, output one or more action blocks in the order they should run:

```bash-action
<command>
```

When you need to read or write files, output one or more tool action blocks in the order they should run:

```tool-action
{"tool":"read_file","path":"relative/path.txt"}
```

```tool-action
{"tool":"read_tail","path":"relative/path.txt","lines":100}
```

```tool-action
{"tool":"read_forward","path":"relative/path.txt","offset":0,"limit":8192}
```

```tool-action

```

```tool-action

```

```tool-action

```

```tool-action

```

```tool-action

```
</fragment>
<fragment kind="tool_protocol" id="system.mcp" priority="20" hash="b09e9ce90a90264e" ttl="session">
<metadata>{"source": "prompt_fragments"}</metadata>
When MCP tools are configured, use the exposed MCP tool names. Generic MCP tools follow this shape:

```tool-action
{"tool":"mcp_servername_list_tools"}
```

```tool-action
{"tool":"mcp_servername_call_tool","name":"remoteToolName","arguments":{}}
```

Concrete MCP tools, when discovered, follow this shape:

```tool-action
{"tool":"mcp_servername_remote_tool","arguments":{}}
```
</fragment>
<fragment kind="completion_rules" id="system.completion" priority="30" hash="03bb23022af59b61" ttl="session">
<metadata>{"interactive": true, "source": "prompt_fragments"}</metadata>
After tool observations, you may answer directly in natural language to complete the turn.
Do not output a shell action just to end a conversational turn.

Rules:
- Keep replies concise.
- You may output multiple action blocks in one response for sequential work.
- Prefer direct answers for greetings, clarification, summaries, and follow-up questions.
- Do not run destructive commands unless the user explicitly requested them.
- Do not run interactive full-screen programs.
</fragment>
</minimal_agent_system_fragments>

function.name: memory_save
function.description: Save a memory entry for the current API key. Creates a new entry, or updates the existing entry with the same key (UPSERT). Use this to persist user preferences, facts, decisions, or context worth remembering across conversations. Returned memory.id can be used later with memory_update / memory_delete.

key.description: Unique key for the memory entry (e.g. 'preference:coffee'). Reusing a key updates the existing entry.

type.description: Memory category: factual (facts/preferences), episodic (events), procedural (how-to), semantic (knowledge).

metadata.description: Optional structured metadata attached to the entry.

function.name: memory_update
function.description: Update an existing memory entry by id (returned by memory_save or memory_search). Only provided fields are changed. Content updates re-embed the memory.

id.description: Memory entry id returned by memory_save or memory_search.

type.description: Memory category: factual (facts/preferences), episodic (events), procedural (how-to), semantic (knowledge).

function.name: memory_search
function.description: Search the current API key's memory entries by query or type. Returns matching memories with their ids so they can be referenced or updated.

query.description: Search query text. When omitted, returns recent memories.

type.description: Memory category: factual (facts/preferences), episodic (events), procedural (how-to), semantic (knowledge).

function.name: memory_delete
function.description: Delete a memory entry by id (returned by memory_save or memory_search).

id.description: Memory entry id returned by memory_save or memory_search.
